 LITTLE ROCK (KATV) — Arkansas is joining 19 other states and the Federal Trade Commission in suing the Dollar General Corporation for using deceptive pricing practices, Attorney General Tim Griffin announced on Monday.
 In an official statement, Griffin said that Dollar General engaged in a long-running practice of charging customers more at the register for prices displayed on shelves, price tags and advertisements.
 He alleges these practices cost customers millions of dollars.
 The other states in the suit include Alabama, Arizona, California, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan, Mississippi, Nebraska, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Utah and Wisconsin.
 “Arkansans shouldn't have to pay more at the register than the price they were promised on the shelf. Businesses have a responsibility to advertise their prices honestly, and those that deceive consumers must be held accountable," Griffin said. "My office will continue cracking down on deceptive practices that hurt Arkansas consumers.”
 The complaint alleges the following:
 Thousands of Dollar General stores have taken advantage of vulnerable shoppers by extracting millions of dollars in unlawful overcharges with insufficient safeguards to prevent the practice.
 Dollar General received tens of thousands of complaints from consumers across the country who say the company did not honor the advertised price, demonstrating widespread consumer harm and confirming that customers nationwide have been charged more than the advertised price.
 Dollar General knows that it harms consumers by charging more at the register than the prices it advertises, as reflected by the numerous complaints it has received.
